page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 128 GB, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual processor. The underlying processor architecture features a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates balanced execution characteristics. Multi-core performance measured via stress-ng scores 15,978.65, while the PassMark CPU test records 26,408.67, both falling within mid-tier percentiles. High memory capacity and cache architecture contribute to strong compression throughput, reaching 35.26 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip tests. Data processing throughput shows 68.36 GB/sec large-block memory writes and 133.34 GB/sec uncached reads, supporting 26.17 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, requiring external network-attached Premium Storage disks for persistent data. This architectural tradeoff reserves memory and host bandwidth primarily for compute operations and volatile state storage, avoiding the overhead of managing ephemeral local drives. In terms of cost efficiency, the instance provides high density in memory allocation relative to core count, making it cost-effective for large stateful processes that do not mandate GPU compute.

Workload fit centers on applications requiring elevated RAM capacities and predictable CPU scheduling. Standard target deployments include in-memory key-value databases like Redis, enterprise relational database management systems, transactional caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and small-scale machine learning inference utilizing AMX extensions.
description: Microsoft Azure E16s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz across 8 physical cores. It provides 128 GB of RAM, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The server includes no local disk storage and no GPU devices, depending instead on Azure Premium Storage for persistent I/O. Performance evaluations show strong gzip compression at 35.26 GB/sec alongside solid memory throughput of 133.34 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, complemented by 26.17 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance presents a cost-efficient resource profile for memory-bound workloads by prioritizing RAM density over dedicated local storage. It is best deployed for in-memory databases, transactional relational databases, large-scale caching services, and enterprise backend applications.
